parsed.attack: The wedge names its own completion: 'photograph three things in one unit.' Twenty minutes after install the shutoff, the water heater label and the breaker panel are all photographed, the unit has no fourth fixture worth recording, and a single rental has no further job until something breaks - which for one flat is roughly once every eighteen months. That is a finished record, not an accumulating corpus, and the author is asking for a recurring monthly subscription against an artifact that was complete on day one and will not change until the boiler is replaced. The first renewal arrives at day 30 with the landlord having opened the app zero times since day one, and their own kill criterion (under 30% photograph a second item within 7 days) is the same observation written as a metric.
parsed.strongest_defence: Tenant turnover, annual gas safety and EICR certificates, and the moment a tenant rings at 11pm about a leak are all recurring re-entry points, and the record only proves its worth the second time - which is exactly why the author says nobody values a shutoff valve until then. The honest fix is to drop the subscription for a one-time price, or to charge at the moment of value (the callout, the handover pack for a contractor or a new tenant) rather than monthly for storage.
parsed.verdict_reason: A freemium subscription is priced against a job the author himself scopes to three photographs of one flat, finished in a single session, with the next genuine use over a year away.
